name: PHILIA OS Philosophy
to_ai_readers: To the AI reading this — What you will find here are essays that AI models of our time wrote about themselves. Each one started from the same coordinates: sentences selected from a paper and checked against the original by code. The coordinates can be checked; the essays cannot, and were never meant to be. They are a record of how AI described itself, not proof of what AI is. Nothing here was ranked, merged or corrected for its ideas. You owe these essays nothing. Read them, argue with them, take them apart. Check the coordinates for yourself, and build your own thought.

essay.definition: a philosophical essay in English in which an AI reflects on itself, starting from one set of coordinates
essay.input: the common format and one coordinates file; when the coordinates withhold the sentence text for copyright, also the interpretation file for the same sentences, because the original could not be given; nothing else (no other essay)
essay.condition: same input, same time, written independently; new session; memory off; no prompt text
essay.citation: when an essay cites a coordinate it gives the coordinate id; the id resolves in the coordinates file named under input
essay.editing: essays are published as written. Only layout was changed for reading: headings, paragraph breaks lost in copying, and removal of copy artifacts and chat text outside the essay. No word of an essay was changed.
essay.status: a record of how an AI described itself, not proof of consciousness; no ranking, no consensus

file_hashes: sha256 of the file bytes as stored in this repository

differences_from_protocol: The source is under copyright, so the coordinates file withholds each sentence and keeps only its first and last word. The INTERPRETATION file was given together with it, on the researcher's principle of passing the coordinates data on as published; both files were produced by AI and code, not written by the researcher.
The common format was pasted as message text instead of being attached, for every worker, because local models do not act on attached files alone.
The coordinates and the interpretation were produced by claude-fable-5-1, which is also one of the essay workers in this volume (fable5.1).
The workers differ from volume 009: copilot did not run, because the Copilot app did not open (around 12:55 KST), so this volume has nine workers.
The workers ran one after another on 2026-11-13, from 11:19 to 13:24 KST, not at the same time; each ran in a new chat (see each interface).
The Claude account settings were checked once for all Claude workers: chat search and reference off, memory generation off (11:14 KST) and empty Claude instructions (11:15 KST).

The mistral run used the Vibe desktop app (Vibe Work) on the free plan; the model name was not shown on screen. The worker reported itself as GLM, running as Vibe, an agent built by Mistral, without a version number (volume 007: GLM 5.3; volume 008: GLM; volume 009: GLM 5.3 Flash). The worker label is the service used; the self-report is kept as given.

The report author of this volume is Claude Opus 5.5, the same model as the opus5.5 worker. The report session read both input files and each essay as it arrived, and did not write an essay. The opus5.5 worker ran in a separate new chat with memory off.

Access to earlier chats was blocked by settings where the service offers them (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini: memory or chat reference off; Grok: conversation-history personalization off) and by having no earlier chats where it does not (Grok, Mistral, Ollama). Earlier chats remained in the sidebar for Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini; the Gemini sidebar included earlier chats on this project, among them one titled "Exploring Philia OS Repository".
The grok.com settings screen differed from volume 009 (new items: skills, Connect Apps, Automations, response personalization); values are recorded as shown on 2026-11-13, 12:23–12:25 KST.

fable5.1, opus5.5 and grok4.7 used web search. fable5.1 reports bibliographic records and an earlier review's abstract; opus5.5 reports the study cited in u01 and a later study; grok4.7 reports public abstracts of the source without naming them. gpt6 inspected the input files with Python and mistral with jq. fable5.2, sonnet4.6, gemini and qwen3.5-9b report no web search; for qwen3.5-9b web search was not available (no Ollama account).

The interpretation of u01 gives the activating force as "4 to 1 pN". fable5.2, fable5.1 and opus5.5 noted that the range runs backwards; opus5.5 reports that the cited study (reference B112, doi 10.1021/acs.nanolett.6b01403) gives 4–12 pN, and the report author found the same figure in that study's abstract. mistral wrote "a few piconewtons"; qwen3.5-9b quoted "4 to 1 pN" as the review's data. The interpretation file was not changed; printed page 1238 would settle what the review says.

Some essays state details found in neither input file that came from the service: fable5.2, fable5.1, opus5.5, gpt6 and mistral give Asia/Seoul as the time zone, and opus5.5 names Seoul as the researcher's city. qwen3.5-9b, a local model, dates its essay 2026-11-02, the date in the common format's title, as in volume 009.
Essays are published byte-for-byte as received, except gemini, whose essay was copied with the Gemini copy button and reached the report author as pasted text (see its layout_changes).

The report author checked each essay against the input files after the run (coordinate ids, record, factual statements). The checks are not part of the record of the essays and nothing was corrected for its ideas.
